# 2 Clement — Chapter 19 (SOPHIA Consensus)

**Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Clement 19
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Consensus Translation

1. So then, brothers and sisters, after the God of truth, I read you an exhortation to attend to the things written, so that both you may save yourselves and the one who reads in your midst.
2. For as a fee I ask of you to repent with your whole heart, granting salvation and life to yourselves. For in doing this, we will lay down a goal for all the young who desire to labor for the sake of piety and the love of God.
3. And let us not, being foolish, be displeased and vexed whenever anyone admonishes us and turns us from unrighteousness to righteousness.
4. For sometimes, as we do evil things, we do not perceive it — because of the double-mindedness and unbelief that dwells in our hearts; and our understanding is darkened by vain desires.
5. Let us practice righteousness, therefore, that we may be saved in the end. Blessed are those who obey these ordinances; even if they endure hardship for a short time in this world, they shall pluck the immortal fruit of the resurrection.
6. Let the godly person not be grieved if they suffer hardship in the present times; a blessed time awaits them.
7. When they come to life again with those who have been raised, they will rejoice forever in a world that knows no grief, having suffered nothing that was ultimately grievous.

---

## Council Notes

- v.1: "After the God of truth, I read you an exhortation" — this phrase establishes a clear hierarchy: God is the primary author of truth; the preacher is subordinate reader/exhorter. Also confirms the document was read aloud in an assembly (cf. 1 Thess 5:27; Col 4:16).
- v.1: "Brothers and sisters" — *adelphoi kai adelphai* — this chapter explicitly addresses both genders, unlike most of the homily. Significant for community composition.
- v.5: "Pluck the immortal fruit of the resurrection" — *karpon athanaton* — fruit harvested at the end of a growing season; resurrection is pictured as harvest.
- v.7: "Those who have been raised" — the preacher envisions a resurrection community including both the newly raised and those already raised; this is consistent with the bodily resurrection argument of chapter 9.
